items.title: Howard Mandel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: And if you follow any one of those musicians through the piece it’s not difficult. Dolphy plays delightful stuff throughout the entire piece. Ornette too. And Freddie Hubbard too and Don Cherry too.

ctx.x: Yeah. I was looking at a statement you had about — someone asked you about free jazz and I liked what you said and I wonder if you could just expand a little. You said, “Free to know a lot, free to be willing to investigate all possibilities, I think that’s what free jazz is about.” I thought that was a really interesting statement because some people including myself, if you said free jazz to me I would think of “Ascension” and Ornette Coleman’s “Free Jazz” and records that are fairly hard to listen to, at least…

Well I think the idea that jazz can be anything is an idea that has been widely accepted in the jazz community. Free jazz could be based on — not free jazz let me say jazz can be based on Balkan rhythms. Jazz can be inclusive of Chinese instruments. Jazz can be electronica. The idea that jazz is not just a three chord improvisation over swing rhythm, I think that idea has been widely accepted. And I think that when Ornette Coleman did the “Free Jazz” album, was it ’62 or ’63, that’s what he was breaking out of,…
Well Dixieland did the same thing.
